record_title: Sharp condition-number frontier for CG residual spikes
scientific_context: For exact conjugate gradients on a real SPD system with spectral condition number kappa, every adjacent Euclidean residual ratio is at most (kappa-1)/(2 sqrt(kappa)). The constant is sharp already in two dimensions. Hence universal stepwise residual monotonicity holds exactly through kappa = 3 + 2 sqrt(2). The same sharp frontier applies to fixed-SPD-preconditioned CG in the M^{-1} residual norm.
limitations: Exact arithmetic, real finite-dimensional SPD matrices, and standard CG for the main theorem. The sharp constant uses the actual global spectral condition number; enclosing spectral bounds can be conservative. Fixed SPD preconditioning yields the result in the M^{-1} residual norm, not ordinary Euclidean residual norm in general. No finite-precision residual-gap claim is made. Global sharpness is realized at the first step; equality at arbitrary later steps is not claimed. Older Lanczos/CG monographs and elimination-factor literature leave residual historical-equivalence risk.

artifact_inventory.description: Deterministic NumPy checks of the two-dimensional equality family, the sharp monotonicity threshold, random rotated-SPD CG steps, and the inverse conditioning certificate.
Verified floating-point sanity-check output, including Python and NumPy versions, random seed, equality errors, threshold checks, and the largest observed normalized residual ratio.
